articles.title: Seedance 2.5 Camera Control: Block Out AI Film Shots in Blender First
articles.excerpt: AI video models are great at pictures and bad at taking direction. Ask for "a slow dolly-in on a mob boss behind his desk, cat on his lap, 76 mm lens" and you get a shot, not your shot. The camera dri…
articles.body: AI video models are great at pictures and bad at taking direction. Ask for "a slow dolly-in on a mob boss behind his desk, cat on his lap, 76 mm lens" and you get a shot, not your shot. The camera drifts, the framing changes between takes, and the actor ends up wherever the model puts him. So we stopped describing the camera and started building it. Every shot below was blocked out in Blender first, with Blender AI : a gray set, stand-in actors, real lenses and a real camera move. Then that blockout drove Seedance 2.5, so the AI video follows our camera frame for frame. This post walks through three of those films: a Godfather-style office scene, a cyberpunk short called Hope , and a wizard-school potions class. Then it covers the exact workflow behind them.
articles.author: GL

articles.title: Stop Giving Channel Bios a Vote in Every Video Search
articles.excerpt: Embedding every exported field gives a creator's biography a vote in every video search. Example: you search for “sourdough starter,” and a bicycle-repair Short becomes a plausible match because its u…
articles.body: Embedding every exported field gives a creator's biography a vote in every video search. Example: you search for “sourdough starter,” and a bicycle-repair Short becomes a plausible match because its uploader's biography mentions baking. Your ingestion code used json.dumps(row) . The biography came along, then aboutChannelInfo brought another copy. Lab note 001: can we keep creator context without letting it speak for every video? An early catch: subtitles indicates caption availability, and captionLanguages lists available tracks. Neither supplies transcript text, so this corpus can support metadata retrieval, not claims about spoken content. What belongs in a video embedding? Start with the text you could reasonably label as describing that individual Short: its title and description.

articles.title: Your generated work email is still a pattern guess
articles.excerpt: A domain can receive mail while your contact's guessed inbox doesn't exist. You're about to connect email to the CRM's verified-email field. The mapping looks harmless. The uncomfortable part is what…
articles.body: A domain can receive mail while your contact's guessed inbox doesn't exist. You're about to connect email to the CRM's verified-email field. The mapping looks harmless. The uncomfortable part is what that checkbox will tell everyone downstream. The Actor constructs an address from a name and company domain, then checks whether that domain can receive mail. A domain check does not verify a person's inbox. Your ingestion needs to preserve that distinction. Start with a finished dataset Separate execution status from contact evidence before inspecting individual rows. A successful run gets you to the diagnosis stage; it doesn't qualify the contacts for outreach. Example: this input searches for marketing leaders and waits for the run to finish.

articles.title: Your hiring chart may measure who posts most often
articles.excerpt: Your Friday investigation needs an industry ranking. On Thursday evening, industry.value_counts() looks reassuringly tidy. The uncomfortable question is whether those bars measure hiring demand or vis…
articles.body: Your Friday investigation needs an industry ranking. On Thursday evening, industry.value_counts() looks reassuringly tidy. The uncomfortable question is whether those bars measure hiring demand or visibility in a recent-results feed. Totaljobs serves anonymous searches newest-first. Relevance ordering requires a signed-in session and can't be combined with the filters, so the Actor always returns newest-first results. A capped collection therefore selects through posting recency. Recently posted adverts can enter the collection while older vacancies remain open beyond its reach. A chart can describe the collected adverts perfectly and still answer the wrong question.

articles.title: OneGraph: grounding Gemma 4's code reviews in a real dependency graph instead of a guess
articles.excerpt: OneGraph: grounding Gemma 4's code reviews in a real dependency graph instead of a guess An LLM code review tool that reads a diff in isolation has a blind spot: it cannot see what else in the reposit…
articles.body: OneGraph: grounding Gemma 4's code reviews in a real dependency graph instead of a guess An LLM code review tool that reads a diff in isolation has a blind spot: it cannot see what else in the repository depends on the lines that changed. It can comment on the diff, but it cannot tell you the function you just touched is called from nineteen other places, three of them in a different service. That is not a hallucination in the usual sense, it is a coverage gap, and it is the gap code-review-graph and the knowledge-graph-over-vector-search approach in this post about replacing grep-based review both set out to close, each in their own way. OneGraph is my attempt at the same problem, built for Hacktoberfest Hack Day Pune x GDG on Campus VU.

articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 22 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The First Green Star, WD J1330+6435 Explanation: Star light, star bright: is there a green star out tonight? Other than the Sun , all stars are so far from Earth that they appear as points in the sky. They are mostly white, but sometimes noticeably red or blue . articles.title: Faster to Science: A Letter to the Science Community
articles.excerpt: NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall.
articles.body: Dear NASA Science Community, NASA Science wants to deliver science faster, so we’re changing how we compete and select missions. On Monday, October 26, we will host a virtual NASA Science Town Hall, from NASA Headquarters, to explain our new Competition Model 2.0 (CM 2.0), and answer your questions. We have heard you. We have listened. We know that the burden of bringing great ideas forward has been too heavy for too long. It has taken years to move mission concepts through the current two-step process. This has often come with contract management challenges, unpredictability, and not enough funding. NASA is committed to doing better — and I’m excited to share with you how we’re making it happen.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.
